bodies.https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2: ATLANTA – Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that the Stone Mountain Memorial Association (SMMA) Board of Directors voted to appoint Christopher "Chris" Sanders as the Association's next Chief Executive Officer. Sanders will succeed Bill Stephens, who has served in the role since 2011 and will officially retire on December 31, 2026."Marty and I appreciate Bill Stephens' many years of service to the Stone Mountain Memorial Association and his commitment to overseeing the park's operations," said Governor Brian Kemp. "On behalf of the State of Georgia, we thank him for his dedication and commitment to this role and wish him all the best in his retirement.""Chris Sanders has a proven record of leadership in both the public and private sectors, and his time serving on the Stone Mountain Memorial Association Board has given him a strong understanding of the park and its operations," continued Governor Kemp. "I'm confident he will bring that experience and perspective to this important role, and I look forward to seeing all he will accomplish as he leads Stone Mountain Park into its next chapter."Christopher Sanders is an executive leader with extensive experience in organizational strategy, economic and community development, stakeholder engagement, public-private partnerships, and board governance. He served as Executive Director of the East Metro Community Improvement District, where he worked alongside business, government, and community leaders to advance infrastructure, economic vitality, public safety, placemaking, and quality-of-life initiatives. Previously, Christopher held roles at the Georgia Department of Revenue and Georgia Pacific.His leadership extends beyond his professional role through service on boards and civic organizations across Georgia. His board service includes the Georgia Charter Schools Association, United Way of Greater Atlanta’s DeKalb County Advisory Board, and the State Bar of Georgia’s District 4 Unauthorized Practice of Law Committee. Through these roles, he has contributed to issues spanning public governance, education, community investment, legal and professional standards, and regional civic leadership.Christopher holds an MBA from the University of Georgia and a BBA in General Management from the University of West Georgia. His leadership development experience includes Leadership DeKalb, the American Enterprise Institute Leadership Summit Network, and the International Downtown Association Emerging Leaders Fellowship. ATLANTA – Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced the following judicial appointments: the Honorable Paul K. Cook to the Superior Court of the Middle Judicial Circuit, filling the vacancy created by the passage of HB 1215 (Act 450) during the 2026 session of the Georgia General Assembly; the Honorable David Ranieri to the State Court of Muscogee County, filling the vacancy created by the resignation of the Honorable Andy Prather; and Alex Shalishali to the State Court of Muscogee County, filling the vacancy created by the passage of HB 1258 (Act 661) during the 2026 session of the Georgia General Assembly.Paul Cook currently serves as a judge on the State Court of Toombs County, a position he has held since January of 2021. He also serves as a judge on the municipal court in six cities, sits by designation on the Superior Court of the Middle Judicial Circuit, and presides over conflict cases in the State Court of Candler County. In addition to his judicial service, he is the sole practitioner at the Cook Law Firm, LLC, in Vidalia, where he handles a variety of cases ranging from criminal defense to family law matters.Judge Cook received his Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Auburn University in 1992 and his Juris Doctor from the Thomas M. Cooley Law School in 1997. While in law school, he served on the Student Bar Association and as a legal intern for an elder law clinic. Motivated by his faith, Judge Cook serves others through charitable activities and volunteer opportunities in his community.Judge Cook and his wife of 32 years, Mary Beth, have two adult sons, Hart and Jase.David Ranieri currently serves as the Chief Judge of the Recorder’s Court of Columbus. He began his legal career in the U.S. Army Judge Advocate General’s Corps. He served as a prosecutor for more than 21 years, handling misdemeanor and felony cases in the U.S. Army, the Muscogee County Solicitor General’s Office, and the Chattahoochee Judicial Circuit District Attorney’s Office. He also spent more than nine years in private practice, primarily handling civil litigation involving personal injury, construction, medical malpractice, transportation, insurance coverage, workers’ compensation, and business disputes.Born and raised in Columbus, Judge Ranieri attended Columbus College before transferring to Mercer University on an Army ROTC scholarship. He graduated cum laude in 1985 with a bachelor’s degree in political science and earned his Juris Doctor from Mercer University School of Law in 1988.Judge Ranieri is the past president of the Columbus Bar Association and currently serves on its executive committee. He is also a member of the Rotary Club of Columbus, serving on its Board of Directors, and is a past chairman of the New Horizons Behavioral Health Board of Directors. He served many years as an instructor in criminal law legal updates and courtroom testimony, volunteers as a high school mock trial judge, and is a graduate of Leadership Columbus.Judge Ranieri and his wife, Katrina, have a blended family of six children and two grandchildren. He attends St. Anne Catholic Church.Alex Shalishali is a shareholder and attorney with Page, Scrantom, Sprouse, Tucker & Ford, P.C., where he has practiced since 2012. His practice focuses on representing local governments and businesses in complex litigation and regulatory matters. He currently serves as the Dougherty County Attorney, where he oversees the county's legal affairs, advises the Board of Commissioners and county staff, and handles a broad range of governmental, transactional, and litigation matters. He previously served as an Assistant Magistrate Judge for the Muscogee County Magistrate Court, presiding over civil matters and criminal arraignments.Shalishali earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Georgia School of Law in 2012 and his Bachelor of Arts in International Affairs, magna cum laude, from the University of Georgia in 2009.Shalishali has been actively involved in the legal profession and his community. He previously served as President of the Fountain City Bar Association and as Chairman of the Board of Trustees for the RiverCenter for the Performing Arts. He currently serves on the Board of Governors of the State Bar of Georgia and the boards of Emanuel Preparatory School of Math and Science and the Columbus Botanical Garden. He is also a graduate of Leadership Georgia's Class of 2016 and a five time Georgia Super Lawyers Rising Star honoree.Shalishali and his wife, Willette, have two daughters. ATLANTA – Governor Brian Kemp today announced that the Georgia Department of Revenue (DOR) will begin distributing funds to local governments as part of the 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant program this week, delivering property tax relief approved by the Governor and the Georgia General Assembly in the AFY2026 Budget."Along with our partners in the General Assembly, we are delivering on our promise to make life more affordable for hardworking Georgians by providing needed relief for homeowners from property taxes," said Governor Brian Kemp. "Because of our commitment to creating jobs and budgeting conservatively, we are able to take steps such as these to keep more money in Georgians' pockets."The one-time program provides eligible Georgia homeowners with an $18,000 reduction in the assessed value of their homesteads for the 2026 tax year. This relief is applied directly to homeowners' property tax bills, reducing the amount they owe. Some homeowners may already see the savings on bills that have been issued, while others will see the relief as local governments continue issuing tax bills."Governor Kemp and the General Assembly have made property tax relief a priority, and we're pleased to begin delivering that relief to Georgia homeowners," said State Revenue Commissioner David Burge. "Our Department has been working closely with local governments across the state to administer this program, and it's exciting to see those efforts translate into real savings for Georgia families."DOR is processing applications and distributing funds to local governments as the required documentation is submitted and verified. Homeowners with a qualifying homestead exemption do not need to submit a separate application to receive the grant. The relief will appear as a reduction on their property tax bill rather than a separate check or direct deposit.Homeowners with questions about their eligibility or the relief reflected on their tax bill should contact their local tax commissioner's office.For additional information, including frequently asked questions, visit dor.georgia.gov/2026-property-tax-relief-grant. ATLANTA – Governor Brian P. Kemp, in consultation with Lieutenant Governor Burt Jones and Speaker of the House Jon Burns, today announced he is extending a state of emergency due to global market volatility and the corresponding suspension of the state's motor fuel excise tax through November 30. With gas and diesel prices remaining high, this action will provide needed relief for Georgians through the Thanksgiving holiday travel period.“With a major holiday coming up and fuel prices still at high levels, I am proud to take this step to keep more money in Georgians' pockets,” said Governor Brian P. Kemp. “Our commitment to fiscal responsibility and stewarding taxpayer dollars has allowed us to act when needed, whether by suspending the gas tax or returning billions to taxpayers through income tax refunds and property tax relief. I'm grateful to our partners in the General Assembly for their support and for standing with us to budget conservatively for times such as these.”This follows the Governor's previous executive orders declaring a state of emergency, which also suspended state weight limits on commercial vehicles, and then extending that state of emergency and also suspending penalties for using off-road "dyed" diesel on roads. Read the Governor's executive order here. Georgia's current motor fuel excise tax is 33.3 cents per gallon for gasoline and 37.3 cents per gallon for diesel. Following the suspension of the state motor fuel tax on September 28, the average price of a gallon of regular gas in Georgia has remained well below the national average, according to AAA. Georgia's average price for a gallon of regular gas is approximately 63 cents below the national average, and the average price for diesel is around 61 cents below the national average. The current average price for a gallon of regular gas in Georgia is $3.66, and the average price for a gallon of diesel is $ 5.72. ATLANTA – The State of Georgia’s net tax collections during the month of September totaled $3.34 billion for an increase of roughly $76.7 million, or 2.3 percent, compared to FY 2026 when net tax collections approached $3.27 billion for the month. Year to date, net tax revenue collections totaled $8.41 billion for an increase of $240.2 million, or 2.9 percent, compared to September 2025, when net tax collections totaled $8.17 billion through three months.The changes within the following tax categories account for September’s overall net tax revenue increase: Individual Income Tax: Individual Income Tax collections during the month of September totaled roughly $1.42 billion, for a decrease of $61.3 million, or 4.1 percent, compared to last year’s total approaching $1.49 billion.The following notable components within Individual Income Tax combine for the net decrease: • Individual Income Tax refunds issued (net of voided checks) increased by $21.6 million or 28.1 percent• Income Tax Withholding payments for September declined by $62 million, or 5.1 percent, from FY 2026• Individual Income Tax Estimated payments increased by $29 million, or 15.3 percent, over September 2025• All other Individual Tax categories, including Income Tax Return payments, were down a combined $6.7 millionSales and Use Tax: Gross Sales and Use Tax collections for the month totaled $1.73 billion, for an increase of $136.8 million, or 8.6 percent, over September 2025. Net Sales and Use Tax increased by $98.8 million, or 13.3 percent, compared to FY 2026, when net Sales Tax revenue totaled almost $741 million. The adjusted Sales Tax distribution to local governments totaled $880.4 million, which was an increase of $100.2 million, or 12.8 percent, from last year’s adjusted distribution total of $780.2 million. Sales Tax refunds decreased by $62.2 million from FY 2026.Corporate Income Tax: Corporate Income Tax collections for September increased by nearly $37.9 million, or 5.9 percent, compared to last year, when net Corporate Tax revenues totaled $642.7 million.The following notable components within Corporate Income Tax make up the net increase:• Corporate Income Tax refunds issued (net of voids) were up $33.1 million, or 66.7 percent, from FY 2026• Corporate Income Tax Estimated payments increased by $126.6 million, or 32 percent, over September 2025• Corporate Income Tax Return payments decreased by $48.2 million, or 45.3 percent, compared to FY 2026• All other Corporate Tax payments, including S-Corp Return payments, were down a combined $7.4 millionMotor Fuel Taxes: Motor Fuel Tax collections for September declined by $0.4 million, or 0.2 percent, compared to FY 2026, when motor fuel tax collections totaled $203.7 million.Motor Vehicle - Tag & Title Fees: Motor Vehicle Tag & Title Fee collections for the month increased by $8.4 million, or 22.1 percent, while Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT) collections decreased by $8.5 million, or 11.9 percent, compared to the previous fiscal year. Atlanta, GA – Governor Brian P. Kemp today issued an updated State of Emergency for all 159 counties in preparation for Hurricane Isaias. The new Executive Order enables emergency management teams to make necessary arrangements and position needed resources ahead of the storm's impact. He has also directed the Georgia Emergency Management and Homeland Security Agency (GEMA/HS) to activate the State Operations Center (SOC) beginning early Friday afternoon."As we always do with weather events, we’re hoping for the best but preparing for the worst," said Governor Brian Kemp. "I encourage all Georgians to take this storm seriously and prepare now by stocking up on food, batteries, flashlights, water, and other necessities in case of severe weather impacting communities Friday night through Saturday."Forecasters expect Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast Friday evening, with potential impact to the state continuing through Saturday. Impacts could include strong wind gusts and heavy rain throughout the state, potentially leading to spin-off tornadoes, downed trees and power lines, flooding, and other effects."As we closely monitor this system, ensuring the safety of all Georgians is our top priority,” said GEMA/HS Director Josh Lamb. “That's why GEMA/HS is working around the clock in coordination with local, state, and federal partners to ensure that we are fully prepared for any potential impacts. All parts of the state could see impacts from this storm, and we have the resources ready to assist them if that is the case."In case of flooding, do not drive or walk through standing water or drive around barricades. Stay away from downed power lines to avoid the risk of electric shock or electrocution. If a tornado warning is issued, storm cellars or basements provide the best protection. ATLANTA – Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that, in consultation with Lt. Governor Burt Jones, Speaker of the House Jon Burns, and Commissioner of Agriculture Tyler Harper, he has amended the State of Emergency Order issued last week to include waiving penalties for the use of off-road "dyed" diesel, providing further relief to Georgia's truckers and farmers. For the duration of the State of Emergency, there will be no state penalties incurred for selling, delivering, or using dyed fuel oil for on-road vehicle use. The average price of a gallon of diesel fuel has decreased by over 42 cents in that same time. Georgia's average price for a gallon of regular gas is currently 51 cents below the national average. The suspension will take effect at 12:01 a.m. on September 29 and run through October 29. The governor's executive order declaring the state of emergency also suspends state weight limits on commercial vehicles, further reducing the cost factored into everyday goods like those bought in grocery stores. Read the governor's executive order here. “Over the past several years, with the help of our partners in the General Assembly, we've been able to give billions of dollars in relief to hardworking Georgians,” said Governor Brian P. Kemp. “We've remained committed to helping them and our small businesses fight through the tough times, and that's why I'm taking this action today to give further relief.”Georgia's current motor fuel excise tax is 33.3 cents per gallon for gasoline and 37.3 cents per gallon for diesel."Over the past four years, we prioritized hardworking Georgians by putting more money back into their pockets and ensuring Georgia's financial stability," said Lt. Governor Burt Jones. ATLANTA – Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has awarded the state $499,385,000 to help communities impacted by Hurricane Helene strengthen the resilience of drinking water and wastewater infrastructure and respond to water-related emergencies. A list of submitted and fundable projects is available on GEFA’s website. GEFA also received funding under the American Relief Act to assist communities in responding to drinking water and wastewater emergencies.The total Helene-related funding awarded to GEFA is distributed across five funding categories:HRF wastewater: $124.9 millionHRF decentralized wastewater (septic systems): $8.96 millionHRF drinking water: $359.5 millionEmergency wastewater: $3.3 millionEmergency drinking water: $2.75 millionThe first group of individual project awards will be presented to the GEFA board of directors for consideration at its November meeting. ATLANTA – Governor Brian P. Kemp today announced he will appoint Stan Wise to the District 5 seat of the Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC), following the resignation of Commissioner Tricia Pridemore, effective September 4. Wise previously served on the Commission for 24 years, from 1995 to 2018, and Chaired the regulatory body multiple times. Pridemore succeeded him as the District 5 representative. Upon being sworn in, he will step down from the Pendleton Group, where he is currently an associate. "We are also grateful for Stan's willingness to return to the PSC, bringing decades of direct experience and wisdom with him," continued the governor. "Thanks in part to his fortitude and far-reaching vision, Georgia has an incredible economic asset in the form of the first nuclear reactors built in the United States in over 30 years. That kind of courage and foresight is what is needed to keep our state the best place for opportunity."Stan Wise is an associate with the Pendleton Group, an Atlanta-based economic development consulting firm. He previously served as a Commissioner on the Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC) from 1995 to 2018, having been elected statewide four consecutive times. He also served as chairman numerous times throughout his tenure on the Commission. U.S. Energy Secretary Ernest Moniz appointed him to the National Petroleum Council in 2016, and in 2003, his regulatory peers elected him President of the National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners.Before being elected to the PSC, Wise served on the Cobb County Commission, the Cobb County Planning Commission, and the Board of Zoning Appeals.
